name: bounded-particles-cpm
title: Smoldyn particles bounded by Cellular Potts (CPM) voxel cells: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the cpm backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (voxel-region outlines traced from the occupancy), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.
experiment: Run the `bounded_particles` composite with backend=cpm on a small patch (~4 cells, seed_per_cell molecules of A and B) for ~18 steps with one scheduled division. Each step: advance the cpm tissue (cells move/deform; one cell divides), then advance each cell's confined Smoldyn sim. Record per step, per cell: molecule positions + counts (A/B/C). Checks: (1) CONFINEMENT -- every molecule lies inside its cell's boundary each step; (2) CONSERVATION -- at the division step, the mother's count equals the sum over its two daughters; (3) REACTION -- A+B<->C relaxes toward the kf/kb equilibrium inside each cell.
outcomes: The flipbook overlay (reports/assets/bounded_particles_cpm.html) -- particles coloured by cell, each inside its cpm boundary, with a step/cell/molecule caption -- is the qualitative artifact; the confinement / conservation / reaction checks are the quantitative ones (pending run).
notes:
One of three parallel studies (cpm / vertex / munk) that run the SAME composite on the
three multicellular substrates, so the particle coupling can be compared across
paradigms. Smoldyn runs via SmoldynRunner (in-process on Linux 3.12, 3.11 subprocess
bridge on macOS).

Behaviour tests: measured value vs pass threshold (code-graded)

question: Can a Smoldyn particle sim be confined inside each Cellular Potts (CPM) cell's moving boundary, split into the two daughters on division, and run A+B<->C to equilibrium inside a living tissue?

study_card.goal: Confine a Smoldyn particle sim inside each Cellular Potts (CPM) cell and split it correctly on division.
study_card.mechanism: The Cellular Potts (CPM) backend gives each cell a moving boundary; a per-cell Smoldyn sim uses it as a reflective surface (A+B<->C), and on division the mother's molecules are partitioned into the two daughter polygons by containment.
study_card.why_before_next: This is the sub-cellular<->tissue composition axis of the atlas: spatially-resolved intracellular chemistry inside cells whose shape, position and number are set by the Cellular Potts (CPM) tissue.
study_card.expected_result: Particles stay inside their Cellular Potts (CPM) cells (confinement) and are split into daughters on division — the particle sim composes faithfully with the tissue.
study_card.main_expert_question: How faithfully does the Cellular Potts (CPM) cell boundary (its emitted footprint) track the true cell geometry that Smoldyn reflects off, especially right after a division?
